principles: Greet every child personally by name and say goodbye to each one individually at the end.
Every session follows the same pattern: arrival, opening circle, play – practise – play, closing circle. Fixed rituals give children security.
Explain briefly (30 seconds at most), then let them play.
Ask questions instead of giving instructions: the children find solutions themselves.
Praise specifically ("Great how you looked up there"), mistakes are allowed.
Drinks break between phases, everyone plays the same amount, nobody waits for long.

opening: Everyone stands in a circle, the coach at eye level (crouch down).
Name the focus of the week in one sentence, ideally as a question.
closing: Team call: hands in the middle, "1, 2, 3 – Germania!"
Collect the equipment together, every child helps.
Say goodbye to each child individually (high five, their name, one sentence of praise).

an-begruessung-eingang.name: Personal Welcome at the Entrance
steps: The coach stands at the pitch entrance and greets every child by name with a high five.
A short personal question: "How was your day?" or "Did you play at the weekend?"
Then the child grabs a ball and plays freely until everyone has arrived.
an-begruessung-eingang.tip: Say a quick hello to the parents too. A child who arrives shyly gets a small job (e.g. carrying cones).

an-eigener-handschlag.name: Personal Secret Handshake
steps: Every child has their own greeting handshake with the coach (e.g. fist bump, high five, elbow bump).
New children invent their handshake themselves at their first session.
Then grab a ball and kick around freely.
an-eigener-handschlag.tip: Children love it when the coach remembers their handshake.

an-offenes-ankommen.name: Open Arrival with Mini Goal Games
steps: Every child is greeted by name on arrival.
A pitch with mini goals is already set up: whoever is there plays 1v1 or 2v2 straight away.
New arrivals simply join in.
an-offenes-ankommen.tip: This way there's no waiting, and latecomers don't disrupt the start.

an-kapitaen-aufbau.name: Captain of the Day Helps Set Up
steps: Every child is greeted by name.
The captain of the day (taking turns, every child gets a go) helps set up and hands out the bibs.
The others play freely on the mini goals.
an-kapitaen-aufbau.tip: Keep a list so every child is captain equally often.

kr-stimmungsdaumen.name: Mood Thumbs
steps: Every child shows with their thumb how they're feeling today: up, middle or down.
Anyone who wants to can add a sentence.
The coach thanks everyone and names the focus.
kr-stimmungsdaumen.tip: Keep an eye on children with a thumbs down during the session and check in with them.

kr-namensball.name: Name Ball
steps: A ball is thrown or passed around the circle.
Whoever passes calls out the name of the child receiving the ball.
Next level: two balls at the same time.
kr-namensball.tip: Ideal at the start of the season or when new children join.

kr-highlight.name: My Highlight of the Week
steps: Taking turns, each child shares something nice from their week in one sentence.
The coach shares one too.
Then introduce the focus.
kr-highlight.tip: Keep it short, one sentence per child at most.

kr-tierbewegungen.name: Animal Moves in the Circle
steps: One child shows an animal movement (frog, stork, bear), everyone copies it.
The others guess the animal.
Take turns until every child has had a go.
kr-tierbewegungen.tip: Gets the little ones moving already in the circle and breaks the ice.

kr-frage-der-woche.name: Question of the Week
steps: The coach asks a question about the focus (e.g. "When is it better to dribble than to pass?").
Two or three children answer.
The question comes up again in the closing circle.
kr-frage-der-woche.tip: Following Horst Wein: the children should discover solutions themselves.

kr-kapitaen-teamruf.name: Captain of the Day Picks the Team Call
steps: The captain of the day is introduced and gets the captain's armband.
He or she chooses the team call or a warm-up game.
Team call together to start.
kr-kapitaen-teamruf.tip: Take turns so every child gets to be in the spotlight once.

ab-lob-runde.name: Praise Round
steps: In the circle: the coach praises every child for one specific thing from the session.
Thumbs feedback: how did you like the session?
ab-lob-runde.tip: During the session, make a note of what each child did well.

ab-beste-aktion.name: My Best Move
steps: Two or three children talk about their best move of the day.
Come back to the question of the week: what did you find out?
A round of applause for everyone.
ab-beste-aktion.tip: Rotate who gets to share so everyone has a turn.

ab-fairplay-kind.name: Fair Play Star of the Day
steps: The children suggest who was especially fair or helpful today.
That child gets a round of applause and gets to lead the team call.
ab-fairplay-kind.tip: Focus on fairness and helpfulness, not on goals.

ab-ruhiger-ausklang.name: Calm Cool-Down
steps: Everyone sits in a circle, ball on their lap, and breathes in and out deeply three times.
Roll the ball over your legs (ball massage).
Quick thumbs vote: what was the best game today?
ab-ruhiger-ausklang.tip: Helps the children calm down before the parents arrive.

ab-ausblick.name: Look Ahead and Dates
steps: Quick feedback: what went well today?
Look ahead to the next session or match day (meeting point, time).
Choose the captain for next time.
ab-ausblick.tip: Also give the dates to the parents.
